description: Space itself looks wrinkled here, starlight crawling in slow convulsions across a seething boundary less than a tenth of an AU wide. Instruments register vacuum energy boiling into transient particle pairs that persist far longer than physics permits. The effect resembles a hedge trained flat against an invisible wall, branches of probability pressed into place.

The Reach expands in lurches, swallowing empty volumes and spitting out matter in altered states. Ships skirting its edge report instruments disagreeing with one another about basic constants. No two crossings have ever taken the same time.

Automated buoys watched the region for decades before anyone dared follow, after buoy telemetry showed them aging at inconsistent rates. The xeno-physical institute at Callidor maintains a permanent watching station at safe remove. Its director famously described the foam as 'a garden someone forgot to finish growing.'

Expansion has accelerated measurably over the past century, and the watching station keeps recalculating its own retreat distance. Every dataset harvested there rewrites at least one textbook. Freight traffic gives it a wide berth and pays handsomely for anyone fool enough to sample its edge.
